no_new_call_note: The live register is still empty, so there was nothing to review or post-mortem this week. On the hunt itself: grain markets (wheat, corn, soybeans) moved limit-up on Black Sea war-risk headlines that were already the lead story on every wire before the move happened, so nothing there could be early. Oil's slide alongside record-thin US distillate stocks is a real divergence, but the physical-buyer response it implies was already being reported as underway, not ahead of it. Precious and industrial metals - gold's ~15% August rally, copper's record high, uranium back above $90/lb - are each real and each already extensively covered by mainstream and trade press for one to several weeks; the moves are behind us, not ahead. Crypto market-structure news (the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, CFTC comments on rules-without-Congress) dates to August 18-20 and is already the subject of law-firm and financial-press analysis, so it is confirmation, not a variant against consensus. Rare-earth and critical-mineral export-control tension is real and multi-sourced but has been a running, well-covered story since at least mid-August with no new dated development this week that changes the thesis. Mega-cap equity stories (Alphabet's first negative free cash flow, Walmart's same-store-sales deceleration) are both already front-page financial-media stories. Nothing found this week was simultaneously new, confirmed by more than one independent source, and still ahead of where the market's attention already sits - so no call was opened. An empty week is counted, not apologised for.
